domain.name: Monitoring, Logging, Analysis, Remediation, and Performance Optimization

learning_design.unlock_rule: A knowledge node unlocks after all required prompts are revealed.
learning_design.mastery_note: Exploration progress is not mastery evidence; quiz attempts remain the scored retrieval signal.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Metrics: numeric time series | Logs: __________ | Events: __________

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: CPU/latency trend → metrics · __________

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: No single source answers __________.

reveal.text: No single source answers every operational question; correlate signals.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Time-series measurements for AWS resources __________.

reveal.text: Time-series measurements for AWS resources and custom workloads.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Namespace → Metric → __________ → Data points

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Use dimensions such as InstanceId to identify a __________.

reveal.text: Use dimensions such as InstanceId to identify a specific resource or slice.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Track a value that AWS does not publish by default” → __________

reveal.text: Custom metric or agent/integration collection. Use this when AWS does not publish the value by default.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Collect system metrics and logs from supported workloads, including __________.

reveal.text: Collect system metrics and logs from supported workloads, including EC2 and container environments.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: CloudWatch agent: telemetry | SSM Agent: __________

prompts.label: ⚡ ACTION
prompts.placeholder: Install/configure the CloudWatch agent and send __________.

reveal.text: Install/configure the CloudWatch agent and send the chosen metrics.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Memory utilization” on EC2 is a clue for __________.

reveal.text: CloudWatch agent. Guest OS metrics such as memory usually require an agent because standard EC2 metrics do not include every OS value.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: A managed Prometheus-compatible service for ingesting, querying, and __________.

reveal.text: A managed Prometheus-compatible service for ingesting, querying, and alerting on Prometheus metrics.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Prometheus/OpenTelemetry-style metrics, often with containerized __________.

reveal.text: Prometheus/OpenTelemetry-style metrics, often with containerized and Kubernetes workloads.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Use CloudTrail for AWS API activity __________.

reveal.text: Use CloudTrail for AWS API activity and audit history.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Records activity performed through AWS APIs __________.

reveal.text: Records activity performed through AWS APIs and related account activity.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use CloudTrail to investigate which identity performed an __________.

reveal.text: Use CloudTrail to investigate which identity performed an AWS action and when.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: CloudTrail: API/audit activity | CloudWatch: __________

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Which identity called Delete/Put/Modify…?” → __________

reveal.text: CloudTrail event history or trail data. Use it to identify which identity made the API call.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: An alarm evaluates metric data and changes state when its __________.

reveal.text: An alarm evaluates metric data and changes state when its configured condition is met.

prompts.label: ⚡ ACTION
prompts.placeholder: Amazon SNS · __________

items: other supported direct targets or EventBridge workflows

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Configure missing-data behavior deliberately; it can affect whether an alarm enters __________.

reveal.text: Configure missing-data behavior deliberately; it can affect whether an alarm enters ALARM, OK, or stays unchanged.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Composite alarms combine other alarms __________.

reveal.text: Composite alarms combine other alarms with Boolean-style rules.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use composite alarms to suppress noisy symptoms and alert only when __________.

reveal.text: Use composite alarms to suppress noisy symptoms and alert only when a meaningful combination is true.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Alert only when CPU is high AND unhealthy hosts exist” → __________

reveal.text: Composite alarm. It can alert on a Boolean combination of other alarm states.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Log event → Metric filter → __________ → Alarm

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Turn matching log patterns, such as errors, into metric data you __________.

reveal.text: Turn matching log patterns, such as errors, into metric data you can graph or alarm on.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: It extracts metric __________.

reveal.text: It extracts metric values from logs; it does not provide general log searching by itself.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Dashboards display metrics, alarms, text, and __________.

reveal.text: Dashboards display metrics, alarms, text, and other operational widgets.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: CloudWatch supports centralized dashboards and __________.

reveal.text: CloudWatch supports centralized dashboards and cross-account/cross-Region observability patterns.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Dashboard: human visibility | Alarm: __________

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: SNS fans a message out __________.

reveal.text: SNS fans a message out to configured subscribers/endpoints.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use SNS when an AWS service needs to publish notifications to __________.

reveal.text: Use SNS when an AWS service needs to publish notifications to one or more subscribers.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: SQS is designed for __________.

reveal.text: SQS is designed for queued message consumption; SNS is pub/sub fan-out.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: EventBridge matches events against rules and sends __________.

reveal.text: EventBridge matches events against rules and sends matched events to targets.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: event bus · __________

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “When this AWS event happens, invoke…” → __________

reveal.text: Amazon EventBridge. Use a rule to route matching AWS events to a target.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Input transformers can extract and reshape event __________.

reveal.text: Input transformers can extract and reshape event data for a target.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Transform the event instead of adding a separate function __________.

reveal.text: Transform the event instead of adding a separate function only to reshape fields.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: The event pattern decides whether __________.

reveal.text: The event pattern decides whether a rule matches; transformation changes what is delivered.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: After retries are exhausted, supported configurations can send failed events __________.

reveal.text: After retries are exhausted, supported configurations can send failed events to a dead-letter queue.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Retesting or recovering event processing by __________.

reveal.text: Retesting or recovering event processing by replaying previously archived events.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Target was unavailable; do not lose failed events” → __________

reveal.text: Retry policy plus a dead-letter queue (DLQ). This helps preserve failed deliveries after retries are exhausted.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Automation runbooks define repeatable steps that __________.

reveal.text: Automation runbooks define repeatable steps that Systems Manager can execute.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Good for standardized operational actions such as restart, patch __________.

reveal.text: Good for standardized operational actions such as restart, patch, snapshot, or configuration remediation.

prompts.label: 🔗 CONNECTS TO?
prompts.placeholder: EventBridge → __________ → AWS resource

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Automation can target groups of managed resources __________.

reveal.text: Automation can target groups of managed resources using supported target selectors.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Rate controls let you cap concurrency and error __________.

reveal.text: Rate controls let you cap concurrency and error tolerance for large-scale automation.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Run remediation across hundreds of instances safely” → __________

reveal.text: Systems Manager Automation targeting with rate controls. Limit concurrency and errors when remediating at scale.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Run Command executes approved commands on managed __________.

reveal.text: Run Command executes approved commands on managed nodes through Systems Manager.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Run Command: execute commands/documents | Automation: __________

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Run commands across selected managed nodes __________.

reveal.text: Run commands across selected managed nodes and collect command status/output.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: A Lambda function can implement custom remediation __________.

reveal.text: A Lambda function can implement custom remediation logic against AWS resources.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use Lambda when the action needs custom code or service API orchestration not covered __________.

reveal.text: Use Lambda when the action needs custom code or service API orchestration not covered by a simpler built-in action/runbook.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Prefer the simpler native mechanism when __________.

reveal.text: Prefer the simpler native mechanism when it meets the requirement.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Current SOA-C03 scope includes Kiro and AWS DevOps Agent as __________.

reveal.text: Current SOA-C03 scope includes Kiro and AWS DevOps Agent as examples in analysis/remediation workflows.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Treat telemetry, permissions, change history, and runbooks as the operational __________.

reveal.text: Treat telemetry, permissions, change history, and runbooks as the operational source material for investigation.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Names Kiro or AWS DevOps Agent in an incident-analysis scenario → know their __________ role.

reveal.text: AI-assisted operations/development. Kiro and AWS DevOps Agent assist workflows but do not replace CloudWatch, CloudTrail, or Systems Manager evidence.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Compute Optimizer produces rightsizing and optimization __________.

reveal.text: Compute Optimizer produces rightsizing and optimization recommendations for supported resources.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use recommendations alongside workload knowledge to __________.

reveal.text: Use recommendations alongside workload knowledge to identify over- or under-provisioning.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Treat recommendations as input to __________.

reveal.text: Treat recommendations as input to an operational decision; validate workload constraints before changing resources.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Correlate instance metrics with EBS, networking, application logs __________.

reveal.text: Correlate instance metrics with EBS, networking, application logs, and instance health signals.

prompts.label: ⚡ ACTION
prompts.placeholder: Identify the constrained resource before resizing __________.

reveal.text: Identify the constrained resource before resizing or changing architecture.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “High CPU sustained” vs “low CPU but slow I/O” require __________ actions.

reveal.text: Bottleneck-specific actions. Optimize CPU, storage, memory, or network based on the actual constraint rather than resizing blindly.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Cluster: low-latency/high-throughput placement | Partition: __________ | Spread: __________

columns.title: Spread
items: small number of distinct hardware placements

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Placement strategy should match the workload’s __________.

reveal.text: Placement strategy should match the workload’s network-performance and failure-isolation needs.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: They influence EC2 placement; high availability still requires an __________.

reveal.text: They influence EC2 placement; high availability still requires an architecture that tolerates failures.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Queue depth and workload I/O pattern also matter __________.

reveal.text: Queue depth and workload I/O pattern also matter when diagnosing EBS performance.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: gp3: general SSD; tune IOPS/throughput | io2: __________ | st1/sc1: __________

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Check the EBS volume characteristics and the EC2 __________.

reveal.text: Check the EBS volume characteristics and the EC2 instance’s EBS bandwidth/IOPS capabilities.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Multipart upload improves resiliency and parallelism __________.

reveal.text: Multipart upload improves resiliency and parallelism for large uploads.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: S3 Transfer Acceleration can improve transfers over long __________.

reveal.text: S3 Transfer Acceleration can improve transfers over long geographic distances when appropriate.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Design access patterns and transfer approach for the workload rather than relying __________.

reveal.text: Design access patterns and transfer approach for the workload rather than relying on one universal tuning knob.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Transfer Acceleration: internet path optimization for S3 transfers | DataSync: __________ | Lifecycle: __________

columns.title: Transfer Acceleration
items: internet path optimization for S3 transfers

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: DataSync is a managed transfer/orchestration option for __________.

reveal.text: DataSync is a managed transfer/orchestration option for supported sources and destinations.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Reduce storage cost as objects age” → __________

reveal.text: S3 Lifecycle rules. Use them to transition or expire objects as they age.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: EFS: managed NFS-style elastic file system | FSx: __________ | S3 Files: __________

columns.title: FSx
items: managed file systems for specific protocols/workloads

columns.title: S3 Files
items: file access backed by S3 capabilities/use cases

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Also consider availability, integration, cost __________.

reveal.text: Also consider availability, integration, cost, and lifecycle requirements.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: EBS is block storage __________.

reveal.text: EBS is block storage attached to EC2; shared file services expose file semantics.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Evaluate EFS performance settings and lifecycle/storage-class __________.

reveal.text: Evaluate EFS performance settings and lifecycle/storage-class behavior for the workload.

prompts.label: ⚡ ACTION
prompts.placeholder: EFS lifecycle management can move infrequently accessed data __________.

reveal.text: EFS lifecycle management can move infrequently accessed data to lower-cost storage classes.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Protocol, latency, throughput, OS/workload fit, and __________.

reveal.text: Protocol, latency, throughput, OS/workload fit, and cost still matter.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Correlate CloudWatch metrics with database-level performance __________.

reveal.text: Correlate CloudWatch metrics with database-level performance information and workload behavior.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use RDS performance tooling/insights to investigate __________.

reveal.text: Use RDS performance tooling/insights to investigate database load and bottlenecks.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Identify whether the bottleneck is query load, connections, I/O, locks, CPU __________.

reveal.text: Identify whether the bottleneck is query load, connections, I/O, locks, CPU, or another constraint before resizing.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: RDS Proxy helps applications use database connections more efficiently and improves __________.

reveal.text: RDS Proxy helps applications use database connections more efficiently and improves connection resilience for supported engines.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Connection pooling can reduce connection churn and __________.

reveal.text: Connection pooling can reduce connection churn and pressure on the database.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Too many short-lived DB connections” → consider __________.

reveal.text: Amazon RDS Proxy. It can help supported RDS/Aurora workloads handle many short-lived database connections.

authoring_notes: Original learning content. Official SOA-C03 exam guide revision 1.1 is the scope authority; the supplied May 2026 study guide was used as a supplementary coverage check and was not copied. Prompt placeholders were revised in v2 so ordinary prompts directly cloze or structurally preview the revealed content. Exam-clue prompts retain certification-style scenario wording and now reveal a direct answer first.
